newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - France steps up arms industry restructuring.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - France steps up arms industry restructuring.

text.p: After a slow start, the French government is racing to catch up with the restructured U.S. arms industry by forming a huge defence electronics group which would rank among the world's biggest.

The government said on Wednesday it wanted to sell the Thomson electronics group to the Lagardere conglomerate, which would merge its Matra missiles unit with Thomson's defence electronics subsidiary Thomson-CSF.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe said the government's decision to choose Lagardere over a rival offer from engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom was "based entirely on defence industry logic."
"We've fallen very far behind in relation to the U.S. aeronautics and defence industries which have been restructuring now for 15 years," a French government official said.

"When the Berlin Wall came down, the Americans were ready. We weren't, and we still aren't. We have to act very, very quickly to make sure we don't get left out," said the official, who spoke to Reuters on condition of anonymity.
Seven of the 10 biggest defence electronics companies are American firms created in a merger frenzy triggered by the end of the Cold War.
The new Thomson Matra entity, with combined annual sales of 62 billion francs ($11.91 billion), would rank second in defence electronics after Lockheed-Martin with $22.9 billion but ahead of Hughes.

The only other European company in the Top 10 is Britain's GEC Plc, whose GEC-Marconi subsidiary had been lined up by Alcatel as a partner for Thomson-CSF in what some analysts viewed as a broader European alliance.

The French government launched the restructuring of the sector in February, when President Jacques Chirac announced that he wanted to merge state-owned Aerospatiale and the family-run fighter manufacturer Dassault Aviation.
The defence company mergers arranged this year ensure that the French industry will play an important role in European defence alliances in the making, analysts say.
Aerospatiale, the French partner in the Airbus Industrie consortium, is trying to close agreements on joint ventures on missiles and satellites with Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG.
Matra's missile partner British Aerospace welcomed the addition of Thomson to their planned venture.

"This opens up some exciting new possibilities for us to further build on the development of European defence industry consolidation," BAe Defence chief executive John Weston told Reuters Financial Television.

Matra specialises in air-to-air missiles with the Magic and Mica weapons, while Thomson-CSF has ground-to-air missiles including the Crotale NG (New Generation) and Starstreak very-short-range missile built with Shorts Brothers Plc, a unit of Canada's Bombardier.

Jean-Marc Baron, a defence specialist at consulting firm KPMG Peat Marwick, said the marriage of Thomson-CSF's radar and communications expertise to Matra's space satellite business would open up a new market for Thomson.
Lagardere has major space interests with its Matra Marconi Space (MMS) joint venture with GEC which it wants to use as a platform for the construction of a European satellite giant.
The vertical integration of detection, communications and weapons turns the Matra-Thomson group into a powerful "systems" producer from a seller of separate products.
The U.S. consolidation has focussed on this sort of vertical integration, with companies such as Hughes not only building missiles and satellites but also operating the satellites.

Defence Minister Charles Millon, looking extremely pleased at the government's decision to go with Lagardere, said on Wednesday that it was "particularly necessary when you see the contraction of defence budgets around the world, and the need for a modern group with the strength needed to compete internationally and export."
Industry Minister Franck Borotra, who was reported in the newspaper Le Monde to have threatened to resign over the Thomson decision, praised the new entity's technological synergies.
($1=5.207 French Franc)
